body: affects the growth plate, and it isn't a hormone or a steroid.
punch: Almost nobody in this space has looked at it.

headline: Everything in this niche
body: Estrogen, androgens, growth hormone, IGF-1. That's the whole framework people use to think about height.
punch: A stimulant sits outside that framework and still shows up.

headline: Methylphenidate
body: Applied to growth plate tissue in vitro it promoted premature growth plate closure. Same endpoint estrogen drives, reached a completely different way.
punch: A non hormonal drug hitting a hormonal endpoint.

headline: Then the clinical data
body: Kids and teenagers on central stimulants for up to 16 years showed reduced body weight and a temporary halt in growth, with implications for final stature.
punch: One of the bigger longitudinal datasets in this whole topic.

headline: Notice the word
body: A halt isn't depletion. Growth suppression that slows the division rate can conserve proliferative capacity, which is the mechanism behind catch-up growth.
punch: Suppressed and spent are different outcomes.

headline: So what's the honest read
body: A real signal from two independent directions. Not a settled quantified effect on adult height, and the in vitro dose may not reflect real prescribing.

headline: Do not stop
body: Untreated ADHD carries serious documented harm to school, relationships and injury risk. Nothing here outweighs that and none of this is individual medical advice.
punch: If this worries you the move is talking to the prescriber. Nothing else.

headline: Why this matters anyway
body: It shows the growth plate reacts to drug classes nobody thought to check. The hormone only framework this niche runs on is incomplete.
punch: The interesting question is what else nobody has looked at.
